A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DLR metric, minimum-projection operator and feature-visualization framework. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite the changed title and substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V2 reports original neural-network experiments on MNIST, CIFAR-10/100 and modular division, alongside toy-model results and statistical summaries in Appendix F.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and adds intermediate-layer comparisons and empirical approximation tests in Appendices I and J.

M1.justification: The core MP operator, DLR definition and Nyström Algorithm 1 are retained. Appendix I adds a limited adaptation to intermediate-layer feature kernels, including flattening convolutional activations. Appendix J newly documents QR orthogonalization, but does not establish that the earlier implementation lacked this step.

E1.justification: The original image-classification, encoded-label, scalar-regression, modular-division and toy-function coverage remains. Appendix J adds a controlled Gaussian-feature scenario with known power-law spectra for evaluating approximation accuracy. Intermediate-layer inspection otherwise uses retained image domains.

E2.justification: The original richness-metric comparisons retain Sinit, parameter norm, NC1 and the within-class covariance trace. V3 additionally compares greedy layerwise training with full backpropagation in Fig. 21 and explicitly evaluates the 'base (no QR)' approximation against QR-based calculation in Fig. 25.

E3.justification: The added analyses introduce substantially different validation procedures: intermediate-layer measurements, staged training with auxiliary classifiers and frozen layers, and approximation evaluation against known population quantities. Appendix J uses 10,000 samples, 1,000 Gaussian features and spectral exponents 1, 2 and 4, with eigenvalue, eigenfunction and subspace error measures. These are new protocols, not evidence that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix I adds analyses of where low-rank structure develops, including intermediate-layer learning-rate and batch-normalization comparisons and a greedy-training control. Appendix J adds spectral approximation tests, a QR/no-QR ablation and analysis of finite-test-set saturation. These investigate diagnostic reliability and layer dependence beyond the analyses already present in v2.

E5.justification: V3 Table 8 newly reports DLR standard deviations for previously presented grokking, learning-rate, weight-decay, architecture, label-shuffling, CNN and batch-normalization experiments. Both versions retain the statement that plotted error bars represent one standard deviation over at least three runs; no increased run count is established.

E6.justification: New results include earlier feature collapse under greedy training, with Fig. 21 reporting 82% versus 94% for backpropagation, and approximation-error and QR findings in Figs. 23 and 25. Most matched original results remain unchanged. However, v3 Tables 3 and 8 report no-shuffling DLR as 0.031, while v2 Fig. 3 and retained v3 Fig. 15 show 0.0031; this is an unresolved reporting inconsistency.

T1.justification: The central definitions, neural-collapse propositions and their proofs are retained. Appendix D.4 adds an anisotropic factorization argument, while Appendix J adds Gaussian eigensystem derivations, formal approximation-error definitions and reasoning about nonorthogonality and finite-sample spans. This substantially expands the mathematical treatment, although the new Eq. (72) incorrectly loses a factor rho_k from Eq. (71).

C1.justification: Both versions claim a performance-independent low-rank richness metric, a connection to neural collapse, complementary feature visualizations, detection of known lazy-to-rich transitions and insights into training factors. V3 emphasizes practical measurement and reorganizes these contributions, but their substantive scope was already present in v2, including its appendices.

C2.justification: V2 briefly identifies last-layer and isotropic-target limitations. V3 substantially develops these boundaries: nonlinear intermediate transformations weaken alignment-based interpretation, anisotropy complicates feature/weight allocation, and finite test dimensions can force misleading projection saturation. It also interprets premature collapse under greedy training and explains why cumulative subspaces can be more reliable than individual estimated eigenfunctions.

D1.justification: V3 adds a project-specific source-code link, finite-matrix metric calculation and cost descriptions in Appendix E, explicit architecture/layer definitions in Fig. 22, and test-set projection and QR procedures in Appendix J. Synthetic-data generation settings are also supplied. The earlier preprocessing, training tables and hardware information are largely retained; these additions primarily expand documentation.

R1.justification: New Appendix G substantially positions the visualization against SVCCA, representational-similarity methods and kernel-based visualization, identifying Canatar and Pehlevan (2022) as particularly close. Additional literature supports discussions of imbalanced neural collapse, intermediate representations and unlearning. This expands substantive research positioning beyond the citation-style and publication-metadata updates.

P1.justification: V3 retitles the paper and extensively revises the abstract, contribution list, experimental narrative and conclusion. It separates the richness metric, experiments and visualization into Sections 3, 4 and 5, transfers substantial material between the main text and appendices, and adds dedicated reproducibility and visualization-related-work sections.

P2.justification: V2 Fig. 2 is split into v3 Tables 1 and 2 and Appendix Fig. 11. Several retained plots move between the main text and appendices, while new Tables 3 and 8 consolidate results and uncertainty. Figs. 18–25 add layerwise plots, architecture diagrams and approximation displays. Conference typography and page layout also change substantially.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2, v3 adds useful diagnostic experiments, uncertainty reporting, implementation guidance and research positioning. However, Appendix E.1 does not reconcile its output-Gram calculation with the defined MP projection, and Appendix J introduces algebra and normalization inconsistencies, including Eqs. (72) and (76). The new summary tables also conflict with retained DLR values. These issues leave uncertain whether the added practical guidance faithfully implements and validates the defined metrics, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment.
